description: The role container docker run command mounts the intent file at /tmp/intent.json read-write, so a role container can rewrite the intent it was given. The intent is input only: no role writes it back.
goal: In sandbox_executor/launcher/containers.py, mount the intent file at /tmp/intent.json read-only by appending :ro to the volume argument, and update the characterisation expectations that pin the exact docker run arguments to the new value. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: A read-only intent mount removes a write path from role containers to host files without changing any role's behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: A test in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_container_launch_characterisation.py builds the docker run command from apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/launcher/containers.py for a real intent file and asserts the volume argument is '<intent path>:/tmp/intent.json:ro'.
The pinned full-command expectation in the same test file is updated to the :ro mount and every other argument is unchanged.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest' and 'uv run task lint' passes.
